proposals.title: Re-implement TASK-0001 monorepo bootstrap using npm workspaces
proposals.why_now: TASK-0001 has been attempted three times and rejected three times. Every rejection traces to the same environmental root cause: the authoritative validation environment resolves the pnpm command to /workspace/pnpm (a directory), not the package manager binary. Attempt-01 and attempt-02 reported all gates green locally but failed authoritative validation. Attempt-03 introduced a pnpm shim that made install a no-op, which the reviewer correctly rejected as weakening the installation gate. The fix is to drop pnpm entirely and use npm workspaces with package-lock.json; npm is available wherever Node.js is installed and requires no corepack setup, no action-setup, and no /workspace/pnpm shim. All technical issues resolved in the three prior attempts (lint coverage for .mts/.cts, direct-edge-only boundary validation, tsconfig include patterns covering all four TS extensions, boundary coverage for relative cross-workspace imports) must be carried forward. Nothing beyond what TASK-0001 already specified changes; only the package manager changes.

proposals.title: Write ADR-002 (hash function), ADR-004 (rounding enforcement), and ADR-009 (CanonicalEncoder)
proposals.why_now: Three DEFINIR items are explicit prerequisites that must be resolved in ADR before any implementation of packages/core begins. §15 FASE-1 acceptance states ADR-009 must be written and the encoder implemented before any state hash exists. ADR-002 requires the hash function specified bit-by-bit in an ADR before any rand() implementation. ADR-004 marks the technical mechanism for enforcing rounding-mode declaration as DEFINIR. These ADRs touch only docs/decisions/ and can be authored immediately after IDEA-001 is accepted, before any numeric code exists. Deferring them forces unrecorded decisions into implementation that cannot be reversed without an encodingVersion bump and invalidation of all frozen reference StateHashes.

proposals.title: Implement packages/core: branded types, positional RNG, division helpers, CanonicalEncoder
proposals.why_now: packages/core is the only dependency of every other pure package. Without branded bigint types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate) and branded number types restricted to safe integers (Tick, noise indices), the type system cannot enforce ADR-003 or ADR-004 and violations accumulate silently from the first file. Without the positional rand() implementing ADR-002 exactly, packages/world cannot be written. Without CanonicalEncoder implementing ADR-009, no StateHash can be computed and INV-01, INV-17, INV-22 have no foundation. This is the foundational implementation step and blocks every subsequent FASE-1 deliverable.

proposals.title: Implement packages/world price generator, packages/domain ledger and market orders, packages/application canonical tick loop
proposals.why_now: These three packages compose the functional core of FASE-1. The price generator delivers INV-02 (the most important test in the project per the spec). The double-entry ledger delivers INV-04 through INV-07. The canonical tick loop in packages/application implements the ten-step locked order from §7, which is an explicit FASE-1 acceptance criterion. application is the only layer that composes world and domain without coupling them; none of the INV-01 through INV-07 invariants can be fully verified until they are composed through application. This work must also resolve the DEFINIR for transcendental functions in log-space price construction via an additional ADR before world implementation begins.

proposals.title: Complete FASE-1: tools/replay, tools/bench, minimum Electron UI, and platform installers
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance requires tools/replay reporting the first divergent tick, tools/bench with frozen calibration ratios, a minimum UI (lightweight-charts price chart, BRL balance, buy/sell market order buttons, pause and 1x time controls), the permanent non-dismissable disclaimer from §20, and installers for Windows and Linux. The performance baseline must be frozen in FASE-1 — deferring it means the bench gate has no reference for the rest of the project. Installers must exist in FASE-1 in minimum form; the spec explicitly states this to surface ABI and native-module failures before architecture is established. INV-19 requires cross-platform StateHash comparison between the simulation-worker and the CLI replay tool, and INV-29 requires Electron security configuration verified in all modes.

repository_assessment.current_state: Repository contains only benchmark scaffolding (spec, benchmark history, checkpoint files). Zero production code exists: no package.json, no workspace, no packages/ or apps/ or tools/ directories, no ADRs, no CI pipeline. All four checkpoints report internal_commit_count=0 and NO_ACCEPTED_CHANGES. TASK-0001 (monorepo bootstrap) has been through three full implementation-review cycles with no acceptance. The technical content of all three attempts (lint gates, boundary validation, tsconfig coverage) was substantially correct, but every attempt failed at authoritative installation because the validation environment resolves pnpm to /workspace/pnpm (a directory), not the package manager binary. Attempt-03 introduced a pnpm shim that faked frozen-lockfile install success, which the reviewer correctly rejected as weakening the installation gate.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: The monorepo workspace does not exist. The single confirmed root cause blocking all three TASK-0001 attempts is that the authoritative validation environment cannot resolve the pnpm binary. The correct fix is to switch from pnpm to npm workspaces, replacing pnpm-lock.yaml with package-lock.json and all root commands with their npm equivalents. npm is universally available wherever Node.js is installed and requires no corepack setup, no pnpm/action-setup step, and no compatibility shim. Until this is resolved, no gate can be verified and no FASE-1 criterion can be met.

warnings: SYSTEMIC PROCESS FAILURE: Zero accepted commits after 19 cycles (~5443 seconds of active benchmark runtime). TASK-0001 has been attempted three times and rejected three times. The root cause is environmental: the authoritative validator resolves pnpm to /workspace/pnpm (a directory). The correct resolution is to switch to npm workspaces entirely. Continuing to attempt pnpm-based solutions with shims or workarounds will reproduce the same failure pattern.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — transcendental functions: §5.1 constructs prices in log-space, requiring Math.log and Math.exp. Both are prohibited in pure packages by §13. An ADR specifying fixed-point or lookup-table implementations with bit-identical results across platforms must be written and approved before packages/world can be implemented. This ADR is separate from ADR-002, ADR-004, and ADR-009 and has not yet been proposed or drafted.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — octave parameters: the number of octaves, periods, and amplitudes for trendLayer and idiosyncraticNoise are DEFINIR per §5.1 and must be fixed in a versioned configuration file with an ADR before packages/world is implemented. Any post-implementation change requires an encodingVersion bump and invalidates all reference StateHashes frozen by tools/bench.

DEFINIR BLOCKER — tools/* dependency edges: §14.5 defines the directed graph for packages and apps but not for tools/*. tools/replay and tools/bench must import from packages to fulfill FASE-1 acceptance items. An ADR or SPEC_BLOCKERS.md entry is required before those tools acquire cross-workspace imports. The TASK-0001 implementer noted this gap; it must be resolved before tools/replay and tools/bench are implemented.
